title: Use WCS EntityLogs (DeveloperLogs) to find OptiSweep application logging evidence for debugging
summary: Use the WCS Entity Logs database (specifically the DeveloperLogs table/model) to locate OptiSweep logging records and use the recorded log attributes (log level, code area/part of code, and line of code) as evidence for debugging.
when_to_use: When you need to find OptiSweep application logging evidence in the WCS Entity Logs database to support debugging, and you want to use the log’s recorded attributes (log level, code area/part of code, and line of code) to pinpoint where the error originated.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as the only step when EntityLogs/DeveloperLogs is missing or contains no relevant OptiSweep entries; escalate to deeper WCS/OptiSweep database support instead.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Connect to the WCS SQL Server database via SSMS, locate the EntityLogs database and DeveloperLogs table/model, and extract the log attributes needed to support debugging.

access_required: SSMS access to the WCS SQL Server instance that hosts the EntityLogs database
system_preconditions: EntityLogs database exists within Fortna’s WCS SQL Server environment

steps.title: Review OptiSweep-related log entries and extract debugging attributes (level, code area, line of code)
steps.purpose: Use the log attributes stored in DeveloperLogs to support debugging by identifying where the log came from (level/part of code/line of code).
steps.instruction: Query or browse DeveloperLogs entries for OptiSweep-related errors, and extract the fields the source says are useful for debugging: log level, what part of the code it came from (code area/part of code), and the line of the code.
steps.expected_result: You have one or more OptiSweep logging records from DeveloperLogs with values for: (1) log level, (2) code area/part of code, and (3) line of code.
steps.healthy_condition: DeveloperLogs records show the debugging attributes described by the source (log level, code area/part of code, and line of code).
steps.failure_condition: DeveloperLogs contains no relevant OptiSweep entries, or the entries do not provide the debugging attributes (level/code area/line of code) needed to support debugging.

steps.title: Use the log evidence to explain where the error occurred (based on logging attributes)
steps.purpose: Translate the DeveloperLogs evidence into a debugging explanation that identifies the code area/part of code and line of code associated with the error.
steps.instruction: Based on the extracted logging attributes from the DeveloperLogs record(s), explain what part of the code produced the error and where it occurred using the recorded code area/part of code and line of code.
steps.expected_result: A debugging explanation is produced that ties the error to the recorded log level, code area/part of code, and line of code from the DeveloperLogs record(s).
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation references the specific logging attributes present in the DeveloperLogs record(s) you extracted (level, code area/part of code, line of code).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot connect the error to the recorded code area/part of code and line of code because those attributes are missing or unusable in the retrieved log entries.

success_criteria: DeveloperLogs records for OptiSweep-related errors are located in the WCS EntityLogs database.
The retrieved records include log level, code area/part of code, and line of code values.
You can produce a debugging explanation that identifies the code area/part of code and line of code associated with the error using those recorded attributes.
healthy_conditions: EntityLogs database is present in the connected WCS SQL Server instance.
DeveloperLogs table/model is present within EntityLogs.
DeveloperLogs entries include the debugging attributes described by the source: log level, code area/part of code, and line of code.
failure_conditions: EntityLogs database is not present/visible in the connected WCS SQL Server instance.
DeveloperLogs table/model is not present within EntityLogs.
DeveloperLogs contains no relevant OptiSweep entries.
Retrieved log entries do not provide the debugging attributes needed (log level, code area/part of code, line of code).
escalation_guidance: If EntityLogs/DeveloperLogs is not present or contains no relevant OptiSweep entries, stop and escalate to deeper WCS/OptiSweep database support (the source only states that OptiSweep uses EntityLogs for logging, not how to remediate missing logs).
